newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan job ratio falls for first time since July 95.
newsitem.headline: Japan job ratio falls for first time since July 95.

text.p: The first fall in Japan's jobs-to-applicants ratio since July 1995 was due to a month-on-month drop in new job openings, a Labour Ministry official said on Friday.
He said the question of whether there would be further drops would hinge on whether new job openings continued to fall and it was necessary to keep a close watch on future movements.

The Labour Ministry said the ratio of job openings to job seekers fell to 0.73 in February from 0.76 a month earlier, with the number of job openings falling 2.8 percent against a 1.3 percent rise in the number of applicants.
This means there were 73 job openings for every 100 job seekers.

The official said that the number of new job openings was still rising in year-on-year terms but the size of the increase had fallen from a month earlier. This, coupled with a large decrease in job openings in the construction sector, had brought the ratio down, he said. The closely watched ratio is seen as a leading indicator of employment conditions in Japan.
